title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: employees, officers and directors
tiers.description: All employees, officers and directors of Patriot; subject to the general Dealing and Communication Prohibitions based on possession of undisclosed Material Information, but not to the additional blackout, pre-clearance, anti-hedging, margin lending or short-term dealing restrictions in Section 5, which apply only to Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders.

tiers.name: Reporting Insiders
tiers.description: All directors and executive officers and certain other members of senior management of Patriot considered to be reporting insiders within the meaning of National Instrument 55-104 - Insider Reporting Requirements and Exemptions.

tiers.name: Designated Insiders
tiers.description: Individuals Patriot designates as subject to certain trading restrictions due to access to Material Information, including key management personnel having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling or reporting Patriot's activities, and family members and closely connected persons of such people who are separately designated by Patriot.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The chair of the Board; distinguished only for the identity of pre-clearance and short-term dealing/short selling approvers.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Patriot; distinguished only for the Australian ASX Listing Rule 3.19A disclosure obligation.

definitions.hedging_definition: engage in transactions in derivatives in respect of Patriot Securities or equity-based incentive arrangements (such as put and call options), or any other hedging or equity monetization transaction in which the individual's economic interest and risk exposure in Patriot Securities or equity-based incentive arrangements is changed (such as collars or forward sales contracts)

windows.start_anchor: two (2) weeks following the end of the prior fiscal year
windows.end_anchor: one (1) trading day after the public disclosure of Patriot's annual financial results or annual report

windows.start_anchor: two (2) weeks following the end of the prior fiscal quarter
windows.end_anchor: one (1) trading day after the public disclosure of Patriot's financial quarterly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The CEO and CFO may from time to time, due to special circumstances such as a material project, event or transaction, designate a discretionary blackout period of any length for such Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders as they determine. Patriot may also impose ad hoc trading restrictions on staff working closely with insiders, finance/strategic planning staff, the next layer of management, IT staff with access to insiders' files, and family members/closely connected persons of insiders. The CFO will endeavour to notify affected persons, but 'even when such notification is not provided, blackout periods will apply as set out in this Policy.'

the CFO may exercise discretion to waive any provision of this Policy as it relates to any employee, officer or director in exceptional circumstances, and on such terms as the CFO considers appropriate, provided that the individual seeking the waiver is not in possession of any Material Information that has not been generally disclosed and that making such an exception would not violate any applicable laws.

exemption_authority: The CFO may, in exceptional circumstances, waive any provision of this Policy (including the anti-hedging and margin lending/secured financing prohibitions) as it relates to any employee, officer or director, on terms the CFO considers appropriate, provided the individual holds no undisclosed Material Information and the waiver would not violate applicable laws; waivers are reported to the Board at its next scheduled meeting. Separately, a written exemption to trade during a blackout period may be granted for court-ordered or other overriding legal/regulatory disposals, specifying the permitted time period for the sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Policy, the CFO may exercise discretion to waive any provision of this Policy as it relates to any employee, officer or director in exceptional circumstances, and on such terms as the CFO considers appropriate.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only route by which the outright bans on hedging and secured financing could be waived for a funded collar; it is a case-by-case discretion, must be reported to the Board, and cannot be exercised while the individual holds undisclosed Material Information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other hedging or equity monetization transaction in which the individual's economic interest and risk exposure in Patriot Securities or equity-based incentive arrangements is changed (such as collars or forward sales contracts)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names 'collars' directly as a prohibited transaction, leaving no room to argue a put/call collar falls outside the hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Subject to Section 5(b) herein, there are no exceptions under which a Reporting Insider or Designated Insider may be permitted to trade during a fixed or discretionary blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if a waiver were obtained, execution, unwind or settlement of a collar or loan could not occur during a blackout period except under the narrow court-order exemption.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any individual who has ceased to be an employee, officer or director of Patriot ... must continue to comply with this Policy, including the obligation to pre-clear any trade and observe the blackout period ... and, in any event, for a period of 30 calendar days from the date of termination.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging and secured financing bans, and pre-clearance obligations, survive a departing director or executive for at least 30 days, affecting timing of any collar unwind around departure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If pre-clearance to trade in Patriot Securities is refused, the Reporting Insider or Designated Insider must keep this decision confidential and not disclose to any other person that the request for pre-clearance to trade has been refused.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for aspects of a structure that could in principle be pre-cleared, a refusal cannot be disclosed to the bank, limiting transparency in structuring discussions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: must not engage in any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Patriot Securities or equity-based incentive arrangements
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The secured financing and hedging bans expressly extend to unvested equity-based incentive arrangements as well as ordinary shares, closing off any vesting-based route to the structure.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar is not permitted under this policy for Reporting Insiders or Designated Insiders: Section 5.E expressly names 'collars' and 'forward sales contracts' as prohibited hedging/equity monetisation transactions, and Section 5.F separately bans any margin lending or secured financing arrangement in respect of Patriot Securities or equity-based incentive arrangements, so both the option legs and the secured loan leg are independently and expressly banned regardless of vesting state. These prohibitions cannot be avoided through the ordinary pre-clearance process, and there are no exceptions permitting trading during a blackout period other than a court-ordered or legally compelled disposal. The only possible route to a collar is a discretionary waiver of these provisions by the CFO under Section 6, available only in 'exceptional circumstances', on terms the CFO sets, provided the individual holds no undisclosed Material Information and the waiver would not violate law; any waiver must be reported to the Board at its next meeting. Restrictions (including the anti-hedging and financing bans) continue to bind a departing director or executive for at least 30 days after termination, and a refused clearance or waiver request must be kept confidential. Absent an individually negotiated and Board-reported CFO waiver, this policy forecloses a bank-funded collar for Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders.
